To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the respondents would like to have more control over the security settings of their devices, that they are willing to accept a more secure environment if the system is easy to use, that they do not want to use biometric authentication methods on their smartphone and that they would prefer a system with gradual security settings.
the user is willing to accept biometric authentication as well as 2D and even 3D gestures as authentication methods for smartphones.
users are not willing to give up usability for security.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the users' perceptions of novel authentication methods?
the user's perception and acceptance of new authentication and security mechanisms for smartphones.
the question of how to improve security on mobile phones and to what extent the user is willing to invest more effort to increase security.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the user is not willing to accept the additional effort for authentication methods that are perceived as too complicated or too time-consuming.
the users are not willing to invest more time or effort to protect their devices.
the user is the weakest link of security and therefore the weakest point of a system that is supposed to be secure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
users are aware of the need for security and are willing to use new methods of authentication but only if these methods are not too complex or cumbersome.
a graded security system based on novel authentication technologies would be a welcome addition to the security features of smartphones.
the user's security awareness and the security culture in general are the main factors that determine the user's acceptance and usage of security mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a graded security system is a very promising way to increase user security and to increase user acceptance for new security methods.
users are willing to invest more effort into securing their smartphone but only if they can see a benefit.
users are not willing to give up their smartphones and the ease of use of smartphones in exchange for a higher level of security.
